newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan mortgage-related fund bought T-bills-sources.
newsitem.headline: Japan mortgage-related fund bought T-bills-sources.

text.p: An investment fund set up as part of a government scheme to solve the financial problems of failed Japanese mortgage companies has recently invested in Treasury bills (T-bills), market sources said on Friday.

The New Financial Stabilisation Fund, which was set up as part of a government scheme to solve the financial problems of failed mortgage companies, is estimated to have bought a total of 200 billion to 300 billion yen worth of T-bills, a trust bank trader said.
The fund tried to buy 400 billion yen worth of T-bills this week, a bond market source said.

"The fund tried to buy 400 billion yen worth of T-bills... But they asked for T-bill issues which the sellers did not have in large amounts, so they probably only acquired a portion of that amount," the market source said.
The fund tried to buy three-month T-bills which are due early next year, the source added.

The trust bank trader said there had been a rumour in the market that the fund would buy the three-month T-bills which the Finance Ministry (MOF) offered through a price competitive auction on Friday.
The market source said the fund is investing in short-term instruments for the time being since long-term interest rates are too low.
"The fund is waiting for (long-term) interest rates to rise. They are investing in short-term instruments until that happens," the source said.

The 159th three-month T-bills were quoted at a yield of 0.305/0.350 percent on Friday, and were last traded at 0.32 percent. On September 2, before such mortgage firm-related funds began pouring money into T-bills, the three-month 155th T-bills were traded at 0.385 percent.
